dataset.name: DataSense (CIC IIoT Dataset 2025)
dataset.note: Public Kaggle CSV mirror of the official CIC processed-feature release (registration-gated at cicresearch.ca).

ml_models.name: Random Forest
ml_models.description: An ensemble of 200 decision trees, each trained on a bootstrapped sample of rows and a random subset of features, voting on the final class. Robust, needs no feature scaling, and gives directly-inspectable feature importances.

ml_models.name: Logistic Regression
ml_models.description: A linear model: one weighted sum of the (standardized) features per class, turned into probabilities via softmax. The simplest possible baseline — if this does nearly as well as the ensembles, the classes are close to linearly separable in this feature space; if it does much worse, the boundary between traffic types is genuinely non-linear.

ml_models.name: Gradient Boosting
ml_models.description: Histogram-based gradient boosting (sklearn's LightGBM-style implementation): builds 200 shallow trees sequentially, where each new tree is trained to correct the errors of all trees built so far, rather than voting independently like Random Forest. Usually the strongest classic-ML performer on tabular data.

ml_models.name: Naive Bayes
ml_models.description: Assumes every feature is independent and Gaussian within each class, then applies Bayes' rule directly — no iterative training at all, just per-class mean/variance estimates. Included as a 'how bad is the floor' reference: network/device telemetry features are clearly not independent of each other, so this tests how much that assumption costs here.

ml_models.name: K-Nearest Neighbors
ml_models.description: Classifies each test window by majority vote among its 5 nearest training windows in standardized feature space — no training phase to speak of, all the cost is at inference time (it has to search all 31,538 training rows for every one of the 13,517 test rows).

ml_models.name: SVM (RBF)
ml_models.description: A Support Vector Machine with an RBF (Gaussian) kernel: finds the decision boundary that maximizes the margin between classes, implicitly projecting the standardized features into a higher-dimensional space where a non-linear boundary becomes linear. Unlike every other model here, training cost scales roughly quadratically with the number of rows, which is why this is the slowest model in the entire lineup to train despite being 'classic' ML.

dl_models.name: MLP
dl_models.description: A fully-connected feed-forward network: every input feature connects to every neuron in the first hidden layer, then the next, etc. No assumption about spatial or sequential structure among the features — it has to learn any useful feature interactions from scratch via dense weight matrices.

dl_models.name: 1D-CNN
dl_models.description: Treats the standardized device/network telemetry features as a 1-dimensional signal and slides learned convolutional filters across neighboring features, looking for local patterns before pooling into a fixed-size representation. As with the MQTTset project, there's no genuine spatial relationship between adjacent feature columns here — this is a fair test of the algorithm on these features, not a fair test of what CNNs are built for.

dl_models.name: GRU (Recurrent)
dl_models.description: A Gated Recurrent Unit, reading the standardized features one at a time as if they were a short time series, carrying a hidden state forward, then classifying from the final hidden state. The features have no real temporal order here (they're a mix of packet-size stats, TCP flag counts, device counts, etc.), so this tests whether recurrent processing helps or just adds overhead on data that isn't actually sequential.

dl_models.name: RNN (Vanilla)
dl_models.description: A plain (Elman) recurrent network — the architecture GRU and LSTM were both built to fix. Reads the standardized features one at a time, carrying a single hidden state forward with a simple tanh update and no gating mechanism at all. Included as the 'how much do the gates actually buy you' reference point against GRU and LSTM — vanilla RNNs are known to struggle with longer sequences due to vanishing gradients, which the gated variants were designed to fix.

dl_models.name: LSTM
dl_models.description: Long Short-Term Memory — the original gated recurrent architecture, and (along with GRU) explicitly named in this project's survey as a common IDS approach. Maintains a separate cell state alongside the hidden state, controlled by input/forget/output gates, which is more expressive (and has more parameters) than GRU's single gating mechanism. Same caveat as GRU/RNN: the features have no genuine temporal order here, so this tests whether that extra gating complexity earns its keep on data that isn't actually sequential.

anomaly_models.name: Autoencoder (Anomaly Detector)
anomaly_models.description: An encoder-decoder network trained ONLY on benign device/network telemetry to reconstruct its own input. It never sees a single labeled attack example. At test time, any window the network reconstructs poorly (high error) is flagged as anomalous — useful for catching attack types the model has genuinely never seen labeled, i.e. zero-day detection.

hyperparams.threshold_rule: 95th percentile of reconstruction error on benign training data
